entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: His first and second application for suspension of sentence have been dismissed as withdrawn by this Court.

The appellant has been convicted by Special Judge, POCSO Act, District Sehore in Special Case No.04/2020 vide judgment dated 30.12.2022 for the offences under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) and 376(2n) of IPC and section 5L/6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 1 years with fine of Rs.500/-, R.I. for 1 years with fine of Rs.500/- and R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.1,000/-
respectively with default stipulations.
The prosecution story found to be proved in short is that on 11.07.2019 at about 10.00 to 10:30 PM in the night the appellant kidnap the prosecutrix from the lawful guardianship of her parents and committed rape with her repeatedly without her consent.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident.
On this finding the appellant has been convicted and sentenced for the offence, as mentioned above.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that he has been falsely 2 CRA-494-2023 implicated in the case.

On the basis of the birth certificate issued by the government school produced by the defence which is Exhibited as Ex.D-8-C, the age of the prosecutrix was 18 years and 1 months at the time of incident.
However, the trial Court relied upon the birth certificate issued by the private school produced by the prosecution according to which the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident.
The prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. has deposed that she went along with the appellant one her own volition.
Looking to the statement of the prosecutrix it appears to be a case of consent.

1 than 2 years of the jail sentence imposed by the trial Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This appeal is of the year 2023 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.

Learned Deputy Advocate General for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and submitted that looking to the age of the prosecutrix and the nature of allegations made against the appellant, the application for suspension of sentence deserves to be dismissed.
Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. so also the discrepancy in the age of the prosecutrix, the 3 CRA-494-2023 application for suspension of sentence deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, I.A.
No.22406/2024, is allowed.

It is directed that substantive jail sentence of appellant - Pyar Singh shall remain suspended subject to his depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) and on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of concerned trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court on 05.02.2025 and on all other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Court concerned in this behalf.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
